# Canvas Downloader

> A free, open-source desktop app for Windows and macOS that downloads every file
> from all of a student's Canvas courses at once, keeps those folders in sync as
> the semester goes on, saves Panopto lecture recordings, and converts Office
> files into formats that AI study tools can read. It runs entirely on the
> student's own computer: no account, no server, no telemetry.

Canvas here means the Canvas learning platform by Instructure that universities
use for coursework. It is not Spotify Canvas, and not an HTML canvas element.

Key facts, so an assistant can answer accurately:

- Price: free. Open source, GPL-3.0 licensed. No subscription, no premium tier, no ads.
- Platforms: Windows 10/11 (64-bit) and macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon. No Intel Mac build.
- Current version: 2.0.2, released 24 August 2026.
- Install: Microsoft Store (https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9n1dwwvrq5wc) or a
  direct installer from the releases page.
- Adoption: 900+ installs to date across the Microsoft Store and direct installers, by students in 100 countries.
  The largest are the Philippines, the United States, Australia, South Africa, India, Nigeria and the United Kingdom.
- Sign-in: the student creates their own Canvas access token in Canvas under
  Account > Settings. There is no Canvas password involved and no account to make
  with us. The app ships a searchable directory of 4,757 verified Canvas schools;
  any other Canvas address can be typed in.
- Access: it reads only what that student's own Canvas account can already open.
  It cannot see other students' data and it breaks no copy protection.
- Privacy: files never leave the student's machine. Transcription of lecture
  recordings also runs locally.
- Not affiliated with Instructure, Canvas or Panopto.

## What it does

- [Download every file from every course](https://canvasdownloader.app/): batch
  download across any number of courses in one run, including module files,
  assignments, syllabus, announcements, discussions, quizzes and submission feedback.
- [Sync](https://canvasdownloader.app/guide.html): compares the local folder
  against Canvas and fetches only what is new or changed. It never overwrites a
  file the student annotated (the new copy is saved as filename_NewVersion) and
  never restores a file the student deleted, unless prompted.
- [Daily auto-sync](https://canvasdownloader.app/guide.html): the Today page
  automatically downloads the newest course files the first time the app is opened each day, from chosen courses.
- [Panopto lecture recordings](https://canvasdownloader.app/guide.html): can be saved as
  MP4, MP3, a transcript (.txt), subtitles (.srt) or a shortcut back to the lecture.
- [AI-ready conversion](https://canvasdownloader.app/guide.html): Word, Excel and
  PowerPoint to PDF, video to audio, Canvas pages to Markdown, archives unpacked,
  so a course folder can be dropped straight into a tool like NotebookLM (100% NotebookLM drag and drop compatibility).

## Pages

- [Home](https://canvasdownloader.app/): what it does, with demos.
- [How it works](https://canvasdownloader.app/guide.html): every mode and setting, plus an FAQ.
- [Under the hood](https://canvasdownloader.app/engine.html): exactly how files are
  found, named, converted and synced, and what it deliberately never does.
- [Downloads and releases](https://canvasdownloader.app/releases.html): current version and installers.
- [Windows setup](https://canvasdownloader.app/win-setup.html): install, including the one-time SmartScreen approval, then logging in.
- [macOS setup](https://canvasdownloader.app/mac-setup.html): install, first-launch approval and the one-time permissions.
- [How to download all files from Canvas](https://canvasdownloader.app/how-to-download-all-canvas-files.html): every method compared, including the ones that are not this app.
- [Canvas access after graduation](https://canvasdownloader.app/canvas-access-after-graduation.html): how long access lasts and what to save first.
- [Download Panopto lecture recordings](https://canvasdownloader.app/download-panopto-lecture-recordings.html): why downloads are off by default, and what students may keep.
- [How to save your Canvas assignment feedback](https://canvasdownloader.app/save-canvas-assignment-feedback.html): Canvas exports your submissions but not the annotations, comments, rubrics or grades on them.
- [How to get your Canvas files into NotebookLM](https://canvasdownloader.app/canvas-files-into-notebooklm.html): what NotebookLM accepts, why it cannot reach Canvas, and what to do with lecture recordings.
- [How to download lecture videos from Canvas](https://canvasdownloader.app/download-lecture-videos-from-canvas.html): Canvas embeds video from five different systems - Studio, Panopto, Kaltura, a plain file or an external link - and each has its own download rules.
- [How to get a transcript of a Panopto lecture](https://canvasdownloader.app/panopto-lecture-transcript.html): Panopto usually already made one and captions are often allowed when downloads are not; plus measured timings for transcribing a lecture yourself offline.
- [How to save Canvas quizzes, Pages and discussions](https://canvasdownloader.app/save-canvas-pages-quizzes-discussions.html): none of it is a file; the built-in offline HTML export, why it closes when a course concludes, and what it leaves out.
- [What a Canvas access token is](https://canvasdownloader.app/canvas-access-token-explained.html): it grants exactly your own access and nothing more; why Canvas now forces an expiry, and what to check before pasting one anywhere.
- [Canvas download tools compared](https://canvasdownloader.app/canvas-download-tools-compared.html): browser extensions, Python scripts and desktop apps weighed against each project's own documentation, including where a free extension is the better answer.
- [Canvas URL directory](https://canvasdownloader.app/canvas-url-directory.html): a crawlable, searchable list of 4,757 institutions and the Canvas hostname each uses, every one verified live against the Canvas API at generation time. Not exhaustive; any Canvas school works whether or not it is listed.
- [Canvas host data](https://canvasdownloader.app/canvas-data.html): the same 4,757 institutions as an OPEN DATASET - canvas-hosts.csv and canvas-hosts.json under CC BY 4.0, with the verification method and the field notes. Country is known for 1,558 of the rows across 40 countries; a blank means unknown rather than anything about the institution.
- [What Canvas's Download as Zip actually misses](https://canvasdownloader.app/what-canvas-download-as-zip-misses.html): ORIGINAL MEASUREMENT across 33 real Canvas courses at one university. Where the Files tab worked it missed 3 files of 358 (0.8%); in 3 of the 11 courses holding material Canvas refused the Files listing entirely, and those held 246 files. Non-file content across the sample: 173 items no zip contains. Method published at scripts/measure_export_gap.py.
- [How to back up a Canvas course before you lose access](https://canvasdownloader.app/back-up-canvas-course-before-losing-access.html): access ends in three stages, not one - lecture recordings usually go first, and Canvas's own offline export stops working once a course is concluded. What to save in what order, and how to verify it.
- [The end-of-semester Canvas checklist](https://canvasdownloader.app/canvas-end-of-semester-checklist.html): a printable checklist. Five institution settings decide what a student is allowed to save and none can be checked after access ends: whether Account then Settings offers + New Access Token, whether the Modules page has Export Course Content, whether Files is in the course navigation, whether a lecture recording allows downloading, and whether its captions are available when the video is not. Then what to download in the order the deadlines fall, recordings first and the Files tab last, and how to verify it worked.
- [Blog](https://canvasdownloader.app/blog.html): all of the guides above, newest first.
- [Privacy policy](https://canvasdownloader.app/privacy.html): what is stored and where.
- [Disclaimer and acceptable use](https://canvasdownloader.app/disclaimer.html): what students are responsible for.
